Anonymize a NONMEM-style dataset

anonymize_dataset.Rd

Creates an anonymized NONMEM-style dataset by renumbering subjects, sampling new covariates, cloning observed dosing/observation designs, and replacing observed concentrations with FeRx-simulated values.

Usage

anonymize_dataset(
  data,
  covariates,
  model_file,
  dictionary = list(ID = "ID", EVID = "EVID", AMT = "AMT", TIME = "TIME", DV = "DV", RATE
    = "RATE"),
  method = c("mice", "lme", "copulas"),
  cat_covs = NULL,
  loq = NULL,
  blq_method = c("remove", "cens"),
  sigdig = 4,
  n_candidates = 1,
  similarity = c("energy"),
  score_on = c("concentration", "covariate"),
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

original NONMEM-style data.frame or tibble.

covariates

character vector of covariates to include in the anonymized dataset. May be character(0) for datasets without covariate columns: covariate sampling is then skipped, and each observed subject's dosing/observation design is cloned (in random order) onto a renumbered subject 1:n before the concentrations are simulated.

model_file

path to a FeRx model file used to simulate concentrations. The file is not used verbatim: a model written to fit the original data usually still describes that dataset, so the simulation runs on a temporary copy adapted to the anonymized dataset. In that copy the [data_selection] block (whose filters refer to original records and columns) and the deprecated [initial_values] block are removed; in the [data] block, path is replaced by the absolute path of the simulation dataset, and a column map is kept only when it renames a sampled covariate (from covariates) whose new name does not collide with a column that remains under its own name after all retained renames are applied (renames are simultaneous, so HTCM = WT with WT = HT is kept). Maps onto or from the structural columns (e.g. AMT = DOSE, DV = lndv) are dropped, because the anonymized dataset already uses the canonical names ID, TIME, EVID, AMT, DV and RATE (plus CMT, MDV, ADDL, II and SS when present in data). A relative [priors] from_fit path is made absolute against the directory of model_file, so it keeps resolving from the copy. Comments (# and //) are handled as FeRx handles them.

dictionary

named list mapping expected NONMEM column names to columns in data. Supported keys are ID, EVID, AMT, TIME, DV, and optionally RATE. Defaults use the same names.

method

time-varying covariate sampler used to resample the covariates. "mice" (default) uses sample_covariates_mice_timevarying(), "lme" uses sample_covariates_lme_timevarying(), and "copulas" uses sample_covariates_copulas_timevarying(). Only "mice" supports categorical covariates; "lme" and "copulas" require all covariates to be continuous.

cat_covs

optional character vector of categorical covariates, in addition to factor and character covariates (which are always treated as categorical). Use this for numerically coded categorical covariates, e.g. SEX = 0/1, so they are not sampled as continuous values. They are returned with their original numeric codes. With method = "mice", a warning is raised for numeric covariates that look like categorical codes (whole numbers with at most 3 distinct values) but are not listed here.

loq

optional numeric limit of quantification. Simulated observations below loq are handled according to blq_method.

blq_method

how to handle simulated observations below loq. "remove" (default) removes the below-LOQ observation rows. "cens" keeps them, sets their DV to 0, and adds a CENS column with 1 for below-LOQ observations and 0 otherwise. If data contains an MDV column, it is recomputed from the simulated data: 1 for non-observation records and observations with a missing DV, 0 otherwise (censored observations keep MDV = 0 and are flagged via CENS).

sigdig

number of significant digits to round the sampled covariates and simulated concentrations (DV) to, via signif(), to further obscure the values. Default 4. NULL disables rounding. Rounding is applied before the loq comparison.

n_candidates

number of independent candidates to draw and score against the observed data, keeping the closest match. Default 1 (no scoring; a single candidate is used). When greater than 1, the candidate with the smallest distance to the observed data (see score_on) is selected. The chosen candidate's score is attached to the result as the "similarity_score" attribute.

similarity

distribution-similarity metric used to score candidates. "energy" (default) is the energy distance between the observed and simulated feature matrices, standardized by the observed spread. Lower is closer. The score is population-level, not per-subject, so it does not push individual simulated subjects toward specific real subjects.

score_on

what to score candidates on when n_candidates > 1. "concentration" (default) scores the simulated concentration-time data: each candidate is fully simulated and its (time, log concentration) observation cloud is compared to the observed concentrations, so the PK simulation is run once per candidate. "covariate" scores only the sampled covariate trajectories (baseline, mean, slope and within-subject SD per continuous covariate; per-subject time fraction in each level per categorical covariate), which is cheaper because the PK simulation is then run only once, on the selected covariate sample.

seed

optional integer seed used for covariate sampling and FeRx simulation. NULL (default) does not seed, so each call draws independently.

...

additional arguments passed to the time-varying sampler selected by method (sample_covariates_mice_timevarying(), sample_covariates_lme_timevarying() or sample_covariates_copulas_timevarying()) and, for "mice" and "lme", on to the internal MICE implementation (e.g. maxit). Every argument must be named and accepted by that sampler. Unknown names (typos, or arguments added in a newer irxforge release) and arguments that anonymize_dataset() sets itself (e.g. id_var, n_subjects) are rejected up front with an "unused argument" error.

Value

anonymized NONMEM-style data.frame, with one block of records per anonymized subject (ID 1:n). Each block is a clone of one observed subject's dosing/observation design, returned ordered by time within subject (a stable sort on TIME, so records sharing a time keep their source order and records with a missing time are placed last). The result carries these attributes:

  • "design_map": a data.frame with one row per anonymized subject and columns ID (the anonymized subject ID) and DESIGN_ID (the ID of the observed subject in data whose design was cloned, in its original type). Use it to relate anonymized subjects back to their source design without reconstructing it from the event records. Note that this mapping links the anonymized dataset to the source subjects, so it should not be shared alongside the anonymized data.

  • "similarity_score": the selected candidate's score when n_candidates > 1, otherwise NULL.
